narrative.overview:
Flightlog is set the way an international airport sets its wayfinding: flat black sign panels hung over a white reading ground, with one colour, airport yellow, reserved for the thing you are walking toward. The next flight is a single yellow overhead band; the history below it reads like a concourse of black section signs with ruled rows beneath. Nothing floats, nothing is rounded, nothing glows. Hierarchy comes from scale and contrast alone: IATA codes and figures set at monumental size in a heavy humanist grotesk, everything else in calm sentence case.

The world is warm rather than technical. Hanken Grotesk is a humanist sans, not a monospace or a condensed departures-board face; pictograms are solid white shapes on black inset plates, the way real terminal signage draws them. The map is a sign-black field where routes are drawn in yellow and airports are white points, and it shares the yellow with the list: hovering or focusing a row lights that row's route and dims the rest.

Density is that of a sign, not a dashboard: few elements, very large, with a fixed 16px gutter. On a phone everything stacks; on a wide screen the map and figure directory hold a sticky left column while the list runs beside them.
keyCharacteristics: One yellow, reserved for wayfinding: the next-flight band, the primary hover state, the lit route.
Flat black sign panels and a white reading ground; the scheme never inverts.
Hard square edges everywhere; no radius, no drop shadows.
Monumental heavy codes and figures in tabular numerals; sentence case for all prose.
Solid white pictograms on black inset plates; arrows locked to the edge they point past.

rules.name: The One Live Sign Rule
rules.body: Yellow marks wayfinding and nothing else: where you go next, what you are pointing at, the route that is lit. It never decorates, never fills a static card, never becomes a brand wash across a page.

rules.name: The Signs Don't Invert Rule
rules.body: The colour scheme is light only (`color-scheme: light`). Black lives on sign panels, white is the reading ground; there is no dark mode.

rules.name: The Red Means Loss Rule
rules.body: Signal red appears only where data is lost or an action failed.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Numerals are tabular everywhere (`font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` on body), so figures, dates and flight numbers align in their columns.

rules.name: The Sentence Case Rule
rules.body: Everything is set in sentence case. Uppercase is reserved for data that is uppercase by nature: IATA codes, flight numbers, booking codes, and the inputs that hold them.

rules.name: The Drawn Arrow Rule
rules.body: Route arrows are a drawn SVG pictogram sized to the text (0.8em), never a typed arrow character; screen readers hear the localised "to" instead.

rules.name: The Fixed Columns Rule
rules.body: List rows are a fixed grid (date, route, airline; plus flight number and booking code from 640px). Columns never reflow or wrap; on narrow screens they drop by priority.

rules.name: The Locked Arrow Rule
rules.body: On a band, the direction arrow sits on its own plate at the far edge it points past, mirroring the pictogram plate at the opposite edge.

rules.name: The Flat Sign Rule
rules.body: Panels are flat signs with hard edges. State is shown by colour change (row to yellow, button to yellow, band to pressed yellow), never by lift or shadow.

dos: Do reserve airport yellow for the next flight, the primary hover state, and the lit route.
Do set IATA codes and totals at monumental extra-bold size with tight tracking and tabular numerals.
Do put pictograms on black inset plates, drawn as solid white SVG shapes.
Do lock a direction arrow to the edge of the band it points past.
Do keep list columns fixed and drop them by priority on narrow screens.
Do keep Delete alone at the foot of the edit page, outlined in red, behind a disclosure and a second confirm.
Do use the 16px gutter on every bar, band, row and section sign.
donts: Don't round corners on panels, buttons, inputs or plates.
Don't add drop shadows or lift on hover; change colour instead.
Don't use yellow as decoration, a static fill, or a brand wash.
Don't add a dark mode or invert the scheme; signs don't invert at night.
Don't show the whole globe ringed by separate stat tiles; the map is framed to the flown world and figures sit in one ruled directory.
Don't set prose in uppercase or use a condensed or monospace departures-board face.
Don't type arrow characters into routes; use the drawn arrow pictogram.
